2016.emphasis_summary: The excerpts are heavily table-of-contents and footnote text, and the substantive content centers on a pay-for-performance design (long-term deferral, retention, and a top-quintile bonus tied to Safety, ROCE, TSR, and shareholder distributions) plus shareholder climate proposals on a 2 degree C warming policy, climate-policy impacts, and hydraulic fracturing.
2016.notable_shifts: First available year in sample; no prior-year comparison.

2017.emphasis_summary: The climate content is now anchored in a methane-emissions proposal (Item 13) and the Board's risk-oversight passage on climate science and policy and the Energy Outlook, while the compensation excerpt carries the Board's opposition to a women's pay-equity report that it frames as 'metrics that measure the progress' toward advancement.
2017.notable_shifts: Versus 2016, the 2 degree C global-warming policy proposal, reserve-replacement-in-BTUs item and hydraulic-fracturing item drop out of the proposal list and a methane-emissions proposal takes their place. The gender-pay opposition also hardens: the 2017 proponent text asks ExxonMobil to 'manage gender diversity like a business imperative with greater emphasis on results,' a phrase that does not appear in 2016.

2018.emphasis_summary: The excerpts shift toward board diversity: a Board Diversity Matrix shareholder proposal, a new Pay Ratio disclosure, and a supporting statement arguing that diverse boards avoid 'groupthink' and manage risk better, while climate content is limited to a single line in the risk-oversight passage.
2018.notable_shifts: Versus 2017, no climate-specific proposal appears in the 2018 proposal list excerpt, and the Board-diversity topic becomes the main governance-and-DEI item (diversity mentions roughly double, from 6 to 12). Pay Ratio appears as its own disclosure section for the first time in the series.

2019.emphasis_summary: The 2019 excerpts carry the densest DEI language in the XOM series, with a board-diversity proposal that cites McKinsey, MSCI and a PwC director survey, alongside Board language on 'the balance, experience, and diversity' of directors and a proposal list that includes a Climate Change Board Committee and a report on Gulf Coast petrochemical investment risk.
2019.notable_shifts: Versus 2018, climate returns as a shareholder-proposal topic (a dedicated Climate Change Board Committee item and petrochemical-risk reporting, with climate mentions rising from 2 to 9) and diversity mentions rise from 12 to 19. The board-diversity argument moves from the proponent's groupthink framing toward external research on financial and governance outcomes.

2020.emphasis_summary: The surviving substance is climate-related board oversight: the risk-oversight passage now refers to the Outlook for Energy and an Energy & Carbon Summary and has the Public Issues and Contributions Committee review 'actions taken to address climate-related risks,' while the proposal list turns to environmental expenditures and petrochemical-investment risk.
2020.notable_shifts: Versus 2019, the Climate Change Board Committee proposal is replaced by a report on environmental expenditures and the board-diversity content drops out of the excerpt (diversity mentions fall from 19 to 3). The climate language becomes more operational, adding explicit climate-related risk language to committee oversight and a carbon-accounting reference (the Energy & Carbon Summary).

2022.emphasis_summary: This is the most emissions-focused year in the early series: the Lead Director letter describes a Scope 1 and 2 net-zero-by-2050 ambition and asset-level emission-reduction roadmaps, and the proposal list includes 'Reduce Company Emissions and Hydrocarbon Sales,' with a populated Board-diversity passage that stresses gender and race/ethnicity diversity without quotas.
2022.notable_shifts: Versus 2020 (2021 has no usable sections), emissions language moves from risk-oversight boilerplate to a stated net-zero target: emission mentions rise from 1 to 10 and GHG/carbon mentions from 3 to 7. Diversity content returns as a substantive, populated section after being absent in 2020, with mentions rising from 3 to 14.

2023.emphasis_summary: The 2023 excerpts are the most carbon-heavy in the series, framing the Low Carbon Solutions business and emissions reduction in the Lead Director letter, and the proposal list covers a new Board committee on decarbonization risk, additional carbon capture and storage, and a reduced executive stock holding period.
2023.notable_shifts: Versus 2022, emission mentions roughly double (10 to 24) and the company's emissions story shifts from a net-zero aspiration to described business build-out (Low Carbon Solutions and CCS), while the shareholder proposals move from emissions reduction and hydrocarbon sales toward governance of decarbonization. Diversity mentions decline from 14 to 9 as the proxy text shifts to 'diversity along with the other requirements' of director qualifications.

2024.emphasis_summary: The excerpts pair the Lead Director's emphasis on 'emissions reductions for hard-to-decarbonize industries' with a proposal list dominated by executive-pay and governance items, including 'Revisit Executive Pay Incentives for GHG Emission Reductions,' an additional pay report on gender and racial equity, and a plastics report, while the human-capital excerpt reports a safety metric (a Lost-Time Incident Rate of 0.02 per 200,000 work hours for 2020-2023).
2024.notable_shifts: Versus 2023, climate activity is now tied to executive pay (a GHG-linked pay-incentive proposal replaces the 2023 decarbonization-committee and CCS proposals), and pay-ratio mentions rise from 1 to 4. The human-capital section also changes from 2023's Board-oversight boilerplate to concrete workforce safety performance data, and the gender and racial pay-equity proposal is a new DEI-linked item.
